newsitem.title: FRANCE: French foreign ministry to shift archives.
newsitem.headline: French foreign ministry to shift archives.

text.p: France's Foreign Ministry is to shift its vast archives, including documents by Cardinal Richelieu and Voltaire, to a bigger library to give researchers more access, a spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

The archives on the Left Bank of the river Seine, including more than 50 km (32 miles) of shelves for documents, 500,000 books, 46,000 treaties and maps, will be moved over the river to the Bibliotheque de L'Arsenal in eastern Paris.

"Researchers would go elsewhere to learn about Europe if we didn't move," said Helene Carrere d'Encausse, head of the society of friends of the diplomatic archives, which she called one of the greatest in the world.

The increasingly cramped library, attached to the Foreign Ministry, has only 50 seats for 6,000 accredited researchers, 40 percent of whom are foreigners. Seventy readers turn up a day on average. The documents will be shifted by the year 2000.

The archives include diplomatic correspondence by 18th century writer Voltaire and dramatist Beaumarchais, who was entrusted with secret missions and shipping arms to American colonies during the War of Independence.
The library also has the personal archives of Richelieu, chief adviser to king Louis XIII in the 17th century.
